findings.highlight: It is his best opposition that began three years ago when he found out the truth.
findings.governingReading: Shinji’s habitual destruction is framed as his desperate resistance undertaken to forgive both himself and Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English omits the psychological accommodation and self-justifying purpose of the behavior.

findings.governingReading: The destruction is the fullest resistance Shinji can muster against the truth he learned.
findings.explanation: The English uses malformed abstract wording that obscures his desperate compensatory act.

findings.highlight: The Matou bloodline came to an end when he was born
findings.evidenceJa: 彼が生まれた時、間桐の血は既に役目を終えていた
findings.governingReading: By the time Shinji was born, Matou blood had already exhausted its hereditary function.
findings.explanation: The English makes his birth the time of the bloodline’s ending and loses the already-completed state.

findings.highlight: The Matou family was a family that passed down secret techniques.
findings.governingReading: He was told that the Matou were a lineage transmitting mysteries and had been a special kind of existence.
findings.explanation: The English preserves transmission of secret techniques but omits their asserted special status.

findings.highlight: to be raised in a special way
findings.governingReading: Shinji took pride in the prospect of living a special life as the child of a special house.
findings.explanation: The English changes his future self-conception into the way he would be raised.

findings.highlight: a girl who had none of her own
findings.governingReading: Shinji had been told his father adopted a girl who had no family or relatives.
findings.explanation: The English leaves the missing object unstated, producing a dangling and unclear phrase.

findings.highlight: to remind himself that he was the Matou heir
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐の後継者を自認していった
findings.governingReading: Through studying inaccessible magic, Shinji increasingly regarded and proclaimed himself the Matou heir.
findings.explanation: The English invents a need to remind himself and treats heirship as established rather than self-ascribed.

findings.evidenceJa: 書物を読む資格はない
findings.governingReading: In Shinji’s hierarchy, Sakura has no qualification or right to read the family’s magical books.
findings.explanation: The English changes exclusion from knowledge into physical trespass in the study.

findings.highlight: would live as a normal human being
findings.evidenceJa: 一般人として生を終えるだろう
findings.governingReading: Shinji imagines Sakura will end her life as an ordinary person without learning the Matou knowledge.
findings.explanation: The English removes the lifelong and terminal scope of his condescending prediction.

findings.highlight: A girl lay in the middle of the room
findings.evidenceJa: 部屋の中央には少女がいる
findings.governingReading: A girl is at the center of the hidden room; the narration does not specify her posture.
findings.explanation: The English adds that Sakura is lying down.

findings.governingReading: Unidentified black things writhe around Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English adds swarm multiplicity beyond the deliberately unidentified scene description.

findings.governingReading: Byakuya gives Shinji a single glance as though looking at a nuisance or intruder.
findings.explanation: The English changes a brief dismissive glance into an overt glare.

findings.highlight: it was not her that was looking down on the other person
findings.evidenceJa: 見下すように同情していたのは自分ではなく
findings.governingReading: The final reversal is that Shinji was not the one pitying Sakura from above; he realizes that role belongs to her in his interpretation.
findings.explanation: The English reverses the subject and says Sakura was not the one looking down, breaking the central humiliation sequence.

findings.evidenceJa: 全てが裏返った足場のまま
findings.governingReading: Shinji returns to the mansion while his entire conceptual footing remains overturned.
findings.explanation: The English literalizes the psychological foundation as an unsteady gait.

findings.highlight: the one who was misunderstood was him
findings.evidenceJa: 勘違いしていたのは自分一人
findings.governingReading: Shinji alone had misunderstood the world and his place in it.
findings.explanation: The English reverses agency and makes him the object of someone else’s misunderstanding.

findings.highlight: It is just that he finally realized his own miserableness.
findings.evidenceJa: 初めから反転した自分
findings.governingReading: He concludes that he himself had been inverted from the beginning and only now recognized his misery.
findings.explanation: The English omits the self-directed culmination of the reversal motif.

findings.highlight: it wasn’t safe to have her over at Emiya’s
findings.evidenceJa: あいつの家にやるのは良くない
findings.governingReading: Shinji says he opposed sending or allowing Sakura to go to Shirou’s house.
findings.explanation: The English invents safety as the reason for his objection.

findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮は監視しなくてはならん
findings.governingReading: Zouken’s stated reason is that Emiya Shirou must be monitored.
findings.explanation: The English shifts surveillance from Shirou to his house.
